title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy — Underwriting Rule on the Number of Residence Policies per Customer
content:
## Rule

Under the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy a customer may hold several HomeGuard policies, one per residence premises. The count is taken across every HomeGuard policy in the customer's name, identified by the customer profile, and not policy by policy.

1. **Which policies count.** Only live policies count: a policy that is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal. A cancelled policy and an expired policy do not count.
2. **Holding cap.** The multi-holding cap is **3** live HomeGuard policies per customer. A new policy is bound only when the customer holds fewer live HomeGuard policies than the cap before that new policy is bound.
3. **Primary residence.** At most **1** of the customer's live HomeGuard policies may carry primary occupancy. Every other live policy must insure a secondary or seasonal residence.
4. **When the cap is reached.** The application is declined, and a live policy must first end before another is bound.

The judgement rests on the company's own policy records for the customer profile (the status of each policy in the customer's name), not on the customer's account of how many policies they hold.

## The cap as a table

| Live HomeGuard policies held before the new one is bound | New policy may be bound |
|---|---|
| 0, 1 or 2 | Yes (the count is below 3) |
| 3 | No — the application is declined |

| Occupancy of the live policies | Permitted |
|---|---|
| No more than 1 carries primary occupancy; the rest are secondary or seasonal | Yes |
| 2 or more carry primary occupancy | No |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- *Hypothetical:* a customer holds two in-force HomeGuard policies and one cancelled HomeGuard policy. The live count is 2, below 3, so a third policy may be bound; since one live policy is already the primary residence, the new one must be a secondary or seasonal residence.
- *Hypothetical:* a customer holds one in-force, one pending-nonrenewal and one bound HomeGuard policy. The live count is 3, which is not below the cap, so a new application is declined until one of those policies ends.

## Points of judgement

- **Does an expired policy use up a place under the cap?** No. Only bound, in-force, pending-cancellation and pending-nonrenewal policies count.
- **Is a pending-cancellation policy counted?** Yes. It is still live until it is cancelled.
